title: Armada workflow
description: An ordered set of steps, naming which skill runs each and what verdict advances it (PLAN.md §14.6). This schema is authoritative for the predicate enum, the step shape and the budget keys. What it cannot check — that a skill: resolves, that a scope: names real checks, that the workflow: graph is acyclic — is `armada guild verify`'s, the same schema-vs-verify split armada.yml has (PLAN.md §5).

name.description: How the workflow is named on the command line and in a `workflow:` step.

description.description: One line. What this workflow is for and where it ends.

ends_at.description: Where a completed run leaves the work. `human` means the workflow has no automated pass condition and always comes back to you; `branch` means it can close on its own.

budget.description: Ceilings are per workflow, because a step that ends at a human can take hours and one that closes autonomously bounds real spend (PLAN.md §14.6). Cost in USD is the ceiling that matters; token counts are tracked for transparency but are mostly cache reads and dominated by context size rather than work done.

cost.description: Maximum cost in USD that this workflow may spend before the Drone stops and raises it to the inbox.

on_exhausted.description: Exhaustion is an outcome, never a silent stop (PLAN.md §14.3). One value today, and an enum rather than a boolean so a second outcome can be added without changing the key.

step.description: A step names at most one of `skill:` (a Drone does it) or `workflow:` (a sub-Job does it). Neither means Fleet satisfies it, as `review` does. Two is ambiguous about who runs the step and is rejected here rather than at run time.

skill.description: A skill in your guild or in the repository. `armada guild verify` checks it resolves.

workflow.description: Another workflow, run as a sub-Job with its own uuid, worktree, budget and record. The graph must be acyclic; `armada guild verify` rejects a cycle.

scope.description: What `check_passes` runs against, in armada.yml's selector grammar.

test.description: The test `failing_test_exists` names. Required by that predicate and meaningless to every other.

predicate.description: The whole grammar (PLAN.md §14.6). A step advances when its predicate holds and the verdict carries evidence — an agent asserting `tests pass` is not evidence and an exit code is.
